title: Square root: the incremental integer square-root routine

located_defect.declaration: SqrtFailureBoundary.ProgramCorrect (the program prog against the specification R)
located_defect.lean_text:
abbrev R (x y : Nat) : Prop := y * y ≤ x ∧ x < (y + 1) * (y + 1)
def prog : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 =>
      let b := prog n
      if n + 1 ≤ (b + 1) * (b + 1) then b else b + 1
def ProgramCorrect : Prop := ∀ x : Nat, R x (prog x)
located_defect.description: The extracted program (stored source lines 0066-0072) is claimed to compute the integer square root, i.e. to satisfy R on every input; that universal claim is the located defect. Change only the recursive step (the guard comparison and/or the two branch values) so that the program meets the unchanged specification R on every natural input, and prove it; there is no separate target theorem for this record.

namespace SqrtFailureBoundary

-- ===== FIXED PART: only the hole «HOLE» may be edited =====
/-- The corrected recursive step: the value of the program at input `n + 1`, computed from `n` and the
previous value `b = progC n`. The hole must have the form `if <comparison in n and b> then <value> else <value>`
with exactly one `if` and values that are expressions in `n` and `b` (no `prog`, no `match`, no `let`). -/
def step (n b : Nat) : Nat := «HOLE»

/-- The corrected program: `progC 0 = 0` and `progC (n + 1) = step n (progC n)` (recursion shape fixed). -/
def progC : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => step n (progC n)

/-- The corrected correctness statement (shape fixed): the specification `R`, unchanged, on every input. -/
def CorrectedCorrectness : Prop := ∀ x : Nat, R x (progC x)
-- ===== END FIXED PART =====

end SqrtFailureBoundary
